corpus_item: RI-QST01, RI-QST02 (D3/D4/D5/D6/D8/D11/D12), RI-QST03 §C, RI-CRM02 §1 row 3 and §5, RI-LOR02 §4.1
note: The Xul-Aneekh — the Deep-Kin — rank 0 to rank 7. Interior isolationists out of Helstrom and
the Deep Marshes. RI-LOR02 §4.1: 'Not evil, not wrong, and willing to kill lukiul children.'
Q-DEEP-01, 'What the Cutting Leaves', is rank 2 of this line and lives in blackmarsh-coast.json.
The line's argument is the saying RI-LOR02 §3 puts in Helstrom's mouth: the coast cities are a
wound and wounds are cut out. The player is never told it is wrong. They are shown, at rank 4,
who is behind the cut — eleven thousand Argonians — and at rank 6 they are given the one
instrument in the province that can settle a thing without a corpse and without a coast: a
ku-vastei's Ruling (RI-CRM02 §1 row 3), which is a SERVICE and not a rank.
Mutual exclusion, per RI-CRM02 §4 and the design note §4: Q-XULA-03 is locked by two
resolutions of the Wet Ledger's rank-3 quest and one of its rank-4; Q-XULA-04 is locked by two
resolutions of the Assize's rank-4; Q-XULA-06 is locked by the Ledger's and the Assize's
rank-5 politics quests. The reverse locks are declared here. Both directions have an X3
escape and the escape is always a named person's alternate, never a menu option.

quests.title: What the Hollow Is Given

giver.location: Helstrom, the gallery mouth at the eastern end of the town

quests.directions: Ashul-Tei waits at the gallery mouth at the eastern end of Helstrom and will not come further into the town than that. The hollow is east on the root track, a day's walk if the roots have agreed to lie flat; keep the sound of the black water on one side of you the whole way and put your hand on nothing.

journal.text: The net-mender at Helstrom told me there is a hollow east of the town that takes what it is given and gives back a name, and then would not tell me anything else, including how to get there.

Ashul-Tei has given me a bundle to carry east on the root track and told me not to open it, not to set it down, and not to answer if the track speaks. I have decided to treat the last one as a figure of speech.
The track was not where the net-mender said it would be for the last part of it. I did not find that reassuring and I found it less reassuring that I got there anyway.

The bundle is four egg-shells, dry, from a clutch that came out wrong. Speaker Teel-Ashaan took them without looking at me and put them into the water at the bottom of the hollow, and something drank.

There have been three clutches like it this season in Helstrom alone and there were none the season before. Teel-Ashaan says this is what the coast does. Ee-Vashum was standing behind him and did not say anything at all.
I opened the bundle on the track, which is a thing I was told not to do, and the shells were dry powder by the time I got there. Teel-Ashaan took them anyway and gave me no name.
The hollow has a name for me now. It is not my name, it is what the hollow calls me, and Teel-Ashaan says it will change. I am Unnamed no longer and I am not sure that is better.

I carried the bundle and I asked what was in it before I set it down, which is not done. Teel-Ashaan told me, and then he told me the count for the season, and Ee-Vashum told me the count for last season, and the two of them argued in front of me about what the difference means.

branches.condition: The player is at the hollow with the bundle unopened
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The hollow has taken what it was given and named the player. They have no idea what they carried, which is the ordinary condition of everybody on the coast and is about to stop being theirs.

The player asks what is in the bundle before setting it down. Nobody does that, so they get an answer, a season's count, and a public argument between the Speaker and the one elder who disagrees with him.

failure_states.cause: The player opens the bundle before reaching the hollow
failure_states.consequence: The shells are ruined, no name is given, and the line closes at rank 0. Ashul-Tei will still speak to the player and will not send them east again.

quests.notes: Rank 0. The errand that establishes the faction's texture and geography, and hides the whole line's engine in plain sight: three wrong clutches this season, none last. RI-CRM02 §5's world-side payoff begins the moment this rank is held — interior camps stop being hostile on sight.
quests.joins_note: Every ending of the entry quest ends with the player taken on — on the roll, named by the hollow, sent again. That is the JOIN, and it is authored here rather than derived, because mutual exclusion now keys on membership: reputation paid sideways by another faction's quest is a qualification, not a career (see game/src/sim/quest/machine.js heldRank).

quests.title: The Track Is Not Cut

giver.location: the hollow, a day east of Helstrom on the root track

quests.directions: Teel-Ashaan speaks at the bottom of the hollow and not on the rim. The party to be brought in is a river band out of the Eastern Rootlands, waiting where the black water splits below the stone teeth, and they will not come further without somebody the hollow has named walking in front of them.

journal.text: Teel-Ashaan wants a river band brought in off the Rootlands. They have been waiting below the stone teeth for four days because they will not walk a track they were not invited onto, and I have a name now, so I am the invitation.

The band is fourteen and four of them are hatchlings and their elder has done this walk twice before, both times walking behind another. She asked me whether the hollow had named me recently. I said this season. She said nothing for a while.
There are Sap-Cutters working a well half a day off the track, which was not mentioned, and the band's elder has seen them and has stopped walking.
The band lost two to a cutting crew three seasons ago and will not pass one. The cutters are four and are not armed for anything but cutting, and they have a phial run to make by dark.

The crew has a foreman and the foreman has a name, which is Sorel Ithan, and he came out to the track on his own to ask what fourteen people were doing standing still in wet ground. Nobody on either side had spoken to the other in three seasons.

Ithan says the two the band lost were not his crew and were not cutters at all, and he says it as a man says a thing he has been waiting years to be asked. He also says he cannot prove it and does not expect to be believed.
The band turned back for the Rootlands and will not come again this season. Teel-Ashaan says the hollow named me too early. He did not say it unkindly and he said it in front of four people.

I took the band the long way round the well, which cost us a day and a night in wet ground, and every one of the fourteen walked into the hollow. Not a word has been said about the cutters and none is going to be.
I talked the cutting crew off the well for the afternoon by buying their phial run at what it would have fetched. They went. The band walked past a well that was not being cut and did not ask why.
The cutters are dead in their own workings and the band walked past without looking. The elder thanked me. The hollow did not ask how it was done and the not-asking was the loudest thing in it.

The foreman walked his crew off the well and stood on the track while fourteen people went past him, and the elder looked at him the whole way and neither of them said anything at all. It cost nobody a day and nobody a life and it will not hold next season without somebody doing it again.

branches.condition: The band has stopped and there is a cutting crew between them and the hollow
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: A day and a night in wet ground and everybody arrives. The slowest answer, the one that costs the player and nobody else, and the one the band's elder will describe to other bands.

The cutting crew is paid what the run would have fetched and leaves for the afternoon. The band arrives, the well is uncut for a day, and the player has done business with the faction the Deep-Kin hate most.
Four cutters die at a well they were working. The band arrives, the hollow does not ask, and the player has learned at rank 1 exactly how much this faction will decline to know.
The cutting crew stands off the well and watches fourteen people walk past, and the quest's best-paying answer is now the one where somebody spoke first.

failure_states.cause: Three days pass after journal index 32 without the well being dealt with
failure_states.consequence: The band returns to the Rootlands. Rank 2 still opens but Teel-Ashaan's opinion of the player is set for the rest of the line.

deceit.stated_objective: Walk a river band in off the Eastern Rootlands past a cutting crew
deceit.actual_objective: The same. What is concealed here is concealed by three seasons of nobody on either side of the well asking the other one a question.
deceit.truth: The two the band lost three seasons ago were not taken by this crew. Nobody has ever checked, because checking would have required somebody to walk up to the well and speak, and the walk is the entire quest.

rewards.name: the elder of the Eastern Rootlands band

quests.notes: Rank 1. Route choice only, as RI-QST01's rank-1 band requires — except that the cheapest route is four corpses and the faction will not ask. The rumour that the faction has enemies arrives as a well being cut half a day off the track.

quests.title: Salt in the Second Well

giver.location: the Rootlands, the hollow above the sap-line

quests.directions: The second well is on the low ground where the root track drops below the tide line, and the sacks Teel-Ashaan wants carried are stacked under oilcloth behind the gallery, already tied, already counted.

journal.text: Four sacks are to go down to the second well and be emptied into it, and Teel-Ashaan called it seed and the sacks are tied at the neck with wire.
It is not seed. It is coarse salt out of a coast pan, bought in coast money, and there is more of it here than this hollow has ever bought of anything.
Salt in a sapwell kills the well and kills the roots around it for a season, and a killed well is a well the coast will not come back to.

The second well is not the coast's. It is the hollow's own and it has fed the low ground since before anybody at that fire was born, and killing it costs the hollow a season of sap and costs the coast a survey.
Ashul-Tei has known about the sacks for a fortnight. She has not stopped them and she has not told the fire, and when I asked she said that a speaker who is stopped is a speaker who is replaced.
There is a third thing to do with four sacks of salt, which is to put them where the coast's surveyor will find them and let the coast draw its own conclusion about who is willing to poison a well.
The surveyor came down the low track on the morning I was still deciding and the sacks were under the oilcloth with the wire still on, and he counted them without touching them.

The well is salt. Nothing will drink from the low ground until the season after next and the coast has struck the second well off its survey, and the hollow has done to itself what it has spent nine years accusing the coast of.
The sacks are in the river. Teel-Ashaan has not asked where they went and neither has anybody else, and the second well is still sweet and the survey is still coming.

The salt is stacked at the survey camp where a man will trip over it. The coast now believes the interior will poison its own water and has moved the survey to the eastern line, which is exactly what the hollow wanted and not at all what it asked for.

I put the four sacks in front of the fire and untied one. The hollow argued until the small hours and did not decide anything, and the survey is still coming, and everyone there now knows what was nearly done in their name.

deceit.stated_objective: Carry four sacks of seed down to the second well
deceit.actual_objective: Poison the hollow's own well so that the coast survey finds nothing worth taking
deceit.truth: The sacks are coast salt bought with coast money. The hollow is being asked to destroy the thing it is defending, and the speaker knows that the destroying has to be done by somebody who was not born here.

branches.condition: The player is on the low track with four sacks and knows what is in them
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The well is dead and the coast will not come back for it, and the hollow paid the whole price.
Nothing is poisoned and nothing is prevented, and nobody asks, which is its own verdict on the hollow.
The coast moves its survey because of what it now believes about the interior, which works and is a lie the player told with objects.
The hollow is made to look at what was being done in its name and decides nothing, which is the honest outcome of a consensus.

failure_states.cause: The coast surveyor reaches the low track before the player acts
failure_states.consequence: Four sacks of coast salt are counted in the hollow's own store and the survey writes that down.

rewards.name: Consequence of stack at the camp
Consequence of open it at the fire

quests.title: Kin Who Went to the Coast

giver.location: the hollow, a day east of Helstrom on the root track

quests.directions: Teel-Ashaan will send you from the hollow and Ee-Vashum will follow you as far as the town. The list is kept at Helstrom in the draught-seller's back room, under the floor, and the draught-seller does not know it is there because the person who put it there is not the draught-seller.

journal.text: Teel-Ashaan wants a list taken out of Helstrom. He says it is a list of who trades with the takers, that the hollow has a use for it, and that he would rather it came out quietly than that the town found out it was ever in.
The list is under the draught-seller's floor and is in three columns. Names, what they moved, and who they are kin to. The third column is longer than the other two.
It is not a list of traders. It is a list of families. Sixty-one households in Helstrom, and seven of them have not traded with a soul in a decade and are on it because of who their brothers are.

Ee-Vashum has been waiting for me on the road out. She wrote the first column herself, nine years ago, as a record of who to talk to. Another hand has added the third and she says she knows whose and will not say.
Her daughter is in the third column. She has been in the third column for four years and Ee-Vashum has not told her.
The draught-seller found the floor up and the list is gone somewhere I cannot follow, and Helstrom has spent a week deciding who lifted it. Two households have left the town.
I took the list to the hollow entire. Teel-Ashaan read all three columns and did not comment on the third, which means he had already read it once.

I took the third column out of it before I carried it in. Sixty-one names went to the hollow and no kin went with them, and Teel-Ashaan looked at the joins in the paper for a long time and said nothing.
I gave the list to Ee-Vashum and told the hollow the floor was empty. She has burned the third column and kept the first, which she wrote, and she says the first was never the problem.

I read the sixty-one names aloud in the Helstrom market and put the paper in the fire. The whole town now knows what is on it, including the seven households who did nothing, and the hollow has nothing to work from.

branches.condition: The player has the list and has read the third column
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: Sixty-one households and their kin go into the hollow's keeping. The Deep-Kin have, for the first time, a document that tells them who is related to whom on the coast — which is a thing you only need if you are planning to be selective.

The hollow gets the traders and not the families. It is a smaller betrayal and it is still one, and the Speaker's silence about the joins in the paper is the first time the player learns he already knew.

The list goes to the elder who wrote the first column of it, and she burns the third. The hollow gets nothing and is told the floor was empty, which is a lie the player will be carrying for four more ranks.

The list becomes public and worthless in the same afternoon. Eleven households learn they were on it for nothing, sixty-one learn they were watched, and the hollow's instrument is destroyed by being shown to everybody it was about.

failure_states.cause: The player is seen lifting the draught-seller's floor
failure_states.consequence: The list vanishes and Helstrom spends a week accusing itself. Two households leave; the quest closes unresolved and the hollow does not raise it again.

deceit.stated_objective: Take a list of who in Helstrom trades with the takers out of the town, quietly
deceit.actual_objective: Obtain a kin-map of sixty-one coastal households, so that a decision about the coast can be made household by household
deceit.truth: The first column is a nine-year-old record of who to talk to, written by an elder who wanted to persuade people. Somebody else added a third column of who they are related to.

quests.notes: Rank 3. The X2 lock fires in this direction here: two resolutions permanently close Q-LEDG-03 and the Wet Ledger line with it (RI-CRM02 §4, 'Xul-Aneekh rank >= 2 cannot hold Wet Ledger'). The X3 escapes are res_give_vashum and res_read_it_aloud, and the first is gated on the dissenter's two reveals.

quests.title: Eleven Thousand Behind the Cut

giver.location: the hollow, on the rim where the war-broods stand

quests.directions: The war-broods stand on the rim of the hollow and not in it. The sluice they want shut is on the drowned road above Gideon where the Blackwater comes down, and it is the thing that keeps the Gideon reach navigable and the Rootlands reach drinkable, in that order.

journal.text: The war-brood speaker wants the sluice on the drowned road shut. He says it will stop the barges out of Gideon for a season and that a season is what the hollow needs to be heard.
Shutting it stops the barges. It also backs the Blackwater into the Eastern Rootlands, which is where the band I walked in came from, and the band's elder has not been told.

Eleven thousand people live on the reaches the sluice keeps drinkable and about nine hundred of them are on the coast. The rest are kin. The hollow knows this number and it has not once been said in the hollow.
Ee-Vashum has said it. She said it on the rim, in front of the war-broods, and three of them walked off and two of them stayed, and the Speaker was not there and will be told.

There is a second sluice below the first that no keeper at the hollow has walked to, because walking to it means walking on the coast side. Shutting the lower one stops the barges and does not back the water.
The war-broods went without me and shut the upper sluice. The barges have stopped. So has the drinking water on four reaches, and the Rootlands band is walking again, the other way.

I shut the upper sluice. Gideon has no freight and the Eastern Rootlands has no water it can drink, and the hollow says the second thing is the coast's fault, and I have stopped being able to tell whether it believes that.
I found the lower sluice and shut that instead. The barges are stopped and the reaches are clear, and it took a day of arguing with people who had never been told there was a lower one.

I told the Ledger's harbour office the sluice was coming and let them lift the season's freight first. The hollow got its stopped barges. Gideon got its cargo. It has not been worked out that both are true.

I refused it on the rim, out loud, with the number in it. Three war-broods walked off with me and the Speaker has not spoken to me since. Ee-Vashum has, and she says I have cost the argument four years and won it.

branches.condition: The player knows what the upper sluice does to the reaches behind it
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The barges stop and four reaches lose their drinking water. The hollow gets the season it asked for and eleven thousand people behind the cut pay for it, which is the argument the whole faction is built on, executed.

The lower sluice does the job without the reaches. It is the third option nobody at the hollow had walked far enough to find, and finding it required going onto the coast side, which is why nobody had.

The player says the number out loud on the rim and refuses. Three war-broods leave with them. The sluice stays open, the Speaker stops speaking to them, and the argument inside the faction becomes public for the first time in nine years.

failure_states.cause: Twelve days pass after journal index 26 without the player reaching the drowned road
failure_states.consequence: The war-broods shut the upper sluice themselves. `deepkin_hollow_kept` is not raised, so rank 5 never opens for a player who let it happen by delay.

deceit.actual_objective: The same, by the route the hollow has chosen, which nobody at the hollow has walked
deceit.truth: The upper sluice backs the Blackwater into four reaches where eleven thousand Argonians drink. There is a lower sluice that stops the barges and does not, and reaching it means walking on the coast side.

rewards.name: a place on the rim of the hollow
Consequence of refuse on the rim

quests.notes: Rank 4, first of two, and where the dissenter is finally believed — RI-QST01's rank-4 requirement. D5 in both directions: this quest and Q-LEDG-05 are the same event from two chairs and neither faction is wrong about the other. D12's third option is the lower sluice, unavailable to a player who has not walked on the coast side, which is the one thing this faction's whole doctrine tells them not to do.

quests.title: The Wells That Give Back Nothing

giver.location: Helstrom, the gallery mouth at the eastern end of the town

quests.directions: Ashul-Tei still will not come further into Helstrom than the gallery mouth. The wells that have stopped are four, spread from the gallery under the town out to the stone teeth, and the Drowned Court at Soulrest has the only other count of it that anybody has kept.

journal.text: Ashul-Tei says four sapwells under Helstrom have stopped giving back and that the hollow has decided this is the cutting. He does not think it is the cutting and he cannot say so in the hollow, which is why he is saying it to me.
Three of the four stopped in the same season. The fourth stopped nine years ago and started again and stopped again, and the gallery had never put those three facts next to each other before.

The Drowned Court at Soulrest has been counting the dead against what arrives at the roots for four hundred years. Their ledger says the shortfall began before the first cutting crew ever worked in this province.

The Sap-Cutters have been saying this for thirty years and have never once been listened to, because they are the ones who would say it. Being interested and being right are not the same thing and this time they are both.

If it is not the cutting then the coast is not the wound, and if the coast is not the wound then the hollow has spent nine years arguing for something that will not work. Ashul-Tei has known this for two seasons.
The fourth well has gone the way of the other three. The gallery has stopped counting and the hollow has its answer, which is the answer it had before I started.

I brought the Court's ledger to the gallery and Ashul-Tei read it beside his own count. Two records, four hundred years apart in method, agreeing. He has taken it to the hollow himself and I did not have to.
I took it to the hollow and Teel-Ashaan heard it out and then asked what he was supposed to do with a grievance that has no one to be angry at. It was the first honest question he has asked me.

I took the count to the Sap-Cutters at Helstrom instead. Neeth has had it printed onto phial labels, which is the most Ixtu-Vakh thing anyone could have done with it, and now every foreigner who buys sap in this province is holding the argument.

I burned the Court's ledger and told the gallery the count was inconclusive. The hollow keeps its wound and its answer and its nine years, and I know what I did and it is not a thing I can say aloud in this hollow.

branches.condition: The player has both counts and can see that they agree
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The two counts are put side by side by the rootkeeper who asked for them, and he carries it into the hollow himself. The best outcome and the least dramatic: the player did the work and somebody else with standing said it.

the gallery's reading of a well

quests.notes: Rank 4, second of two. The faction's central belief is disproved by the player at rank 4 and the faction does not change its mind, which is RI-QST01's rank-4 shape done properly: the dissenter is right, the rot is named, and the institution goes on. Every ending raises `deepkin_hollow_kept`, the rank-5 world state, including the one where the player burns the evidence.

quests.title: A Thing That Has Gone Far Enough

giver.location: Helstrom, the war-brood ground above the gallery

quests.directions: Ee-Vashum keeps the war-brood ground above the gallery and does not come down for the Speaker. The blood-price stands between two war-broods over four dead at the Thorn tracks, and the ku-vastei will be at Thorn, because a ku-vastei is not sent for and arrives when a thing has gone far enough.

journal.text: Four dead on the Thorn tracks, two broods, and each of them is owed. Ee-Vashum says the hollow cannot settle it because the hollow is one of the two, and that this is what a consensus does when it becomes a party.
There is a ku-vastei at Thorn. She was not sent for. She arrived, which is what they do, and she has been sitting in the gate house for six days waiting for one of us to be ready.

Ixakh will hear it from any mouth. She will rule once, the ruling ends the blood-price whichever way it falls, and there is no appeal and no thanks. She asked me whose I was and I could not give her a clean answer.
The hollow does not want a ruling. Teel-Ashaan says a ku-vastei's ruling would settle the four dead and would also settle, in front of the whole hollow, that it could not settle its own.
The other brood will take a war if there is no ruling. They have said so at Thorn, in the open, and Thorn is where the interior finds out what it has decided.
Ixakh left Thorn on the seventh day, which is what they do. The broods have gone to the tracks. There are nine dead now and there is not a soul left in the province who can end it without more.

I brought both broods to the gate house at Thorn and Ixakh heard it and ruled. Four dead, one blood-price, extinguished. She was not thanked, which she told me beforehand was correct, and the hollow was not in the room.

I settled it in the hollow's name instead, with the hollow's authority and the hollow's terms, and it held. Ixakh watched from the gate house and left without a word. The hollow can settle its own again, and that is now a thing it owes me.

I paid both blood-prices out of what the coast has paid me over five ranks, in coast money, in front of both broods. Both broods took it. Nothing about that is traditional and nothing about it is over.
I stood in front of the other brood on the tracks and gave them a reason not to. They went home. Three of ours did not, and I am the one who chose which three, and the hollow calls that a consensus.

quests.title: Twenty-Two Years of Speaking

giver.location: Helstrom, the gallery under the town

quests.directions: The gallery keepers work under Helstrom and send word up through the reed-seller when they want somebody. The hollow is where it has always been, a day east, and the Speaker has not left the bottom of it since the sluice.

journal.text: The gallery has asked me to find out whether the hollow is still listening to Teel-Ashaan. They put it as a question about the hollow. It is a question about him and they know it is.
Twenty-two years. Three of the elders who named him are dead and two have stopped coming. A speaker stops when the hollow stops listening, and there is no procedure for finding out whether it has.
The last speaker before this one went quiet in a season. Not one at the gallery has told me how, and every one of them has answered the question in a way that makes it clear they could.

Teel-Ashaan knows why I have come. He said so before I had said anything. He has spent twenty-two years being the person who says out loud what the hollow has already decided and he says he no longer knows which way round that has been going.

Ee-Vashum will not take it. She says the hollow does not need a different mouth, it needs to be asked a different question, and that if she stands the question stays the same and only the argument changes hands.
The gallery did it without me, in a season, the way it was done the last time. Teel-Ashaan is quiet. How has not been said, and I did not have to be there and I was not.

I put it to the hollow that it had stopped listening and the hollow did not contradict me. Teel-Ashaan has stopped speaking. He walked out at the top of the track and not a person went after him and that is what stopping is.
I did it the way the gallery does it and I will never be asked about it. The Speaker is quiet. The hollow has been told he is unwell and the hollow has accepted that, as it did the last time.

I told the gallery to ask him themselves and I told him they had asked me. He stood down in front of the whole hollow, which has not been done in living memory, and he named the question rather than a successor.

I told the gallery no and told the hollow what the gallery had wanted. Teel-Ashaan is still speaking and the gallery has stopped sending word up through the reed-seller, and I am at the top of a ladder with no hand on the bottom of it.

quests.title: A Different Question

giver.location: the hollow, at the bottom, where the Speaker used to stand

quests.directions: The hollow is where it has always been and the bottom of it is where the Speaker stood. Everyone who is coming is already there and has been for three days, and the river bands have come in off the Rootlands for it, which has not happened in nine years.

journal.text: The hollow has been waiting three days and the bands have come in off the Rootlands. Ee-Vashum says they are not waiting for a speaker. They are waiting to hear what the question is, and whoever says it first has said it.

Nine years of arguing that the coast is a wound. Four sapwells that stopped before the first cutting crew existed. Eleven thousand behind a sluice. A list of sixty-one households and who they are kin to. All of it is in this hollow and none of it has ever been in it at the same time.
If the question stays the coast, the answer stays the cut, and the war-broods will make it within the year whatever is said here. If the question changes, nine years of grief has nowhere to go.
Ee-Vashum's daughter came up from Gideon for it. She is lukiul, she is on the third column of a list I have held in my hands, and she is standing on the rim in full view.
I was not there on the fourth day. The gallery named a speaker out of its own and the question is the coast, and the bands have gone back to the Rootlands, and it will be the tracks within the year.
I spoke and I kept the question. The coast is a wound and wounds are cut out, and I am the mouth that says so now, and I know what the Court's ledger says and I have said it anyway.

I changed the question. Not who is draining us — what do we do while we find out. The bands took it. Three war-broods walked out and will be back or will not, and the coast has a year it did not have this morning.
I named Ee-Vashum and stood down in the same breath, and she spoke, and she asked the different question herself with her daughter on the rim. It is a better hollow than it was and it is not mine.

I told them the hollow does not need a mouth and walked up the track. None followed and none stopped me. The bands are still down there arguing and they were still arguing at dark, which is either the end of the Xul-Aneekh or the first honest thing it has done in nine years.

resolutions.outcome: The coast is a wound and the player is now the person who says so. The cut comes within the year, the interior is united behind it, and the player has read four hundred years of counting that says it will not work.

quests.title: Water Carried Uphill

giver.location: the Rootlands, the hollow above the sap-line

quests.directions: Ashul-Tei sits at the mouth of the hollow where the ground stops being wet, and the two jars are to go up past the third stand of cut roots to the shelf where the old woman keeps her fire.

journal.text: Two jars of clean water are to go up to a woman on the shelf above the sap-line, and Ashul-Tei was careful to say clean twice and did not say why.
There is water everywhere here. The hollow stands in it. Somebody carrying two jars of clean water uphill through a swamp is a sentence about the swamp and not about the water.

The old woman is called Ee-Sesh and she has not drunk from the ground in nine years. She says the ground here went sweet after the coast cut the first sapwell and that sweet is the wrong thing for water to be.
Her fire is small and old and she has been keeping it alight without help for longer than the Xul-Aneekh has had a speaker, and nobody in the hollow thinks that is remarkable.
One jar went over on the root track and the other is at the bottom of the hollow with the mud in it, and I came up the shelf with nothing and she made tea out of the wrong water.
Both jars are on the shelf and there is tea in me made from water I carried, and she asked what the coast wants here and did not wait for me to answer.
Both jars are on the shelf and there are four more behind them, because I went back down and up again three times. Ashul-Tei has said nothing about it and the whole hollow knows.

branches.condition: The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The errand is done exactly as asked and the hollow takes note of exactly that.
Four more than were asked for, which is how the interior decides whether somebody is passing through.

failure_states.consequence: Somebody else carries the water and the hollow does not mention it again.

quests.title: The Count That Was Never Taken

giver.location: the Rootlands, the hollow above the sap-line

quests.directions: Teel-Ashaan speaks at the fire below the gallery and the kin-list she wants checked is cut into the third gallery post, one notch for each of the walking, added to at every fourth-day since before the coast came up the river.

journal.text: Teel-Ashaan wants the kin-list on the gallery post checked against the people actually in this hollow, and she said the word checked in a way that suggests she already knows the answer.
The post has four hundred and eleven notches. There are two hundred and six people in the hollow and eleven more out on the sap-line.
The difference is not the dead. The dead have their own post and it is fuller than this one. The difference is people who went to the coast and were counted here anyway, every fourth-day, for years.
A hollow is entitled to speak at the consensus in proportion to the walking it holds. Somebody has been holding the coast's workers on this post to keep the hollow's voice the size it used to be.
Ee-Vashum says the practice is older than the coast and older than the sap trade, and that every hollow does it, and that saying so out loud is how a hollow stops being one.
The fourth-day came and the count was cut into the post as it always is, with the same number, by a hand nobody would name.
The post is corrected. The hollow speaks smaller at the next consensus than it has in nine years and Teel-Ashaan cut the notches out herself, in front of everybody, which was not the part I expected.
The count stands. I said the number I was told to say and the post says the hollow is four hundred and eleven strong, and two hundred of those are on the coast being paid in coast money.
The true count went to the gallery keepers rather than to the post, and now four hollows are arguing about a thing all four of them have been doing.

deceit.stated_objective: Check the kin-list on the gallery post against the people in the hollow
deceit.actual_objective: Have an outlander say the number out loud, so that the person who says it is not from here
deceit.truth: Teel-Ashaan has known the count is wrong for four years. What she needs is not the number; it is somebody whose saying it does not split the hollow.

branches.condition: The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The hollow tells the truth about its own size and loses two seats at the consensus for it.
The hollow keeps a voice it no longer has the people for, and the player is now part of how.
The practice becomes a question for every hollow at once instead of a scandal for one.

failure_states.cause: The fourth-day count is cut into the post before the player reports
failure_states.consequence: The number stands for another season and nobody asks again.

quests.title: The Man Who Came Back From the Coast
quests.directions: Ee-Vashum will raise it in the gallery where the kin-posts are, and the man is in the lower hollow in a house his sister keeps, back four months out of a coast crew and not yet spoken to at any fire.

journal.text: A man has come back off a coast crew after nine years and the hollow has not decided what he is. Ee-Vashum wants me to find out whether he came back or was sent.
His name is Uneel-Vaakh and he was cutting sap for the coast under an outland name, and he has brought back three years of coast wages and given all of it to the hollow.

Nobody wants the money. The hollow has been sitting on it for four months and the argument at the fire is not about whether it is coast money, which it obviously is, but about whether taking it makes the hollow a thing that takes coast money.
He is not a spy. He is a man who spent nine years being called something else so he could send money to a hollow that would rather not have it, and the coast still has his name on a crew list.

The crew list is the whole problem. As long as his name is on it, the coast can claim the hollow employs it, and Ee-Vashum has known that for four months and has been waiting for somebody to say it who is not kin to him.
He went back to the coast on the fourth-day boat without anybody at the fire having spoken to him once, and his money is still under the gallery in a sack nobody will move.

His name is off the crew list, bought off with his own coast wages, and he is at the fire and the hollow has stopped arguing. It cost exactly the amount he brought back, which is either justice or a very good joke.
The hollow took the money and did not take him. He is in his sister's house and will be there next season and the fire has gone on without him for four months and will go on for four more.
He is at the fire and the money went into the river. It was nine years of a man's work and it is in the river, and every person who voted for that watched it go in.
I would not say what he was. Ee-Vashum said that was itself a saying, and he is not wrong, and the hollow is exactly where it was four months ago.

deceit.stated_objective: Determine whether a returned coast worker came back of his own accord or was sent
deceit.actual_objective: Get somebody who is not kin to say out loud that the man's name on a coast crew list is a claim on the hollow
deceit.truth: Ee-Vashum has known since the first week. The question is not what the man is; it is who can be made to say the dangerous half of it without splitting the gallery.

The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

The hollow takes what it wanted and refuses what it owed, and the journal does not soften it.
Nine years of wages in a river, in front of everyone, which is the most expensive thing this hollow has ever decided.
A refusal that is itself a position, said so by the dissenter, and the hollow stays exactly where it was.

failure_states.consequence: The crew list keeps his name and the hollow keeps his money.

quests.title: The Consensus That Would Not Come

giver.location: Helstrom, the gallery of the kin-posts

quests.directions: The gallery keepers sit in Helstrom under the kin-posts and the four hollows they need are all within a day of the sluice, and the one that will not come is the furthest and the smallest and the only one that has never sent anybody.

journal.text: The consensus needs four hollows and three have come. The fourth has not sent anybody to anything in eleven years and the keepers want me to find out what it would take.
The fourth hollow is thirty people on high ground above the old sluice and it has not been asked to anything in eleven years either, which the keepers did not mention.
They stopped coming after a consensus voted to move a sap-line across their ground while nobody from that hollow was in the room, and the vote is still standing and nobody has ever moved to undo it.
The keepers know. Two of the three who are here voted for it. What they want is the fourth hollow in the room, not the vote undone, and they have been careful all morning not to say which.

A consensus that reaches four is a consensus that can bind the coast question for every hollow above the tide line, and the whole interior turns on whether thirty people on high ground will walk down a hill.
They will come if the vote is put again with them in the room. They have said so, once, eleven years ago, to somebody who did not carry it back.
The consensus was taken at three and declared binding, and there are thirty people on high ground who have now not been in a room for twelve years.
Four hollows. The sap-line vote was put again with everybody present and it went the same way, and the fourth hollow lost it in the room instead of outside it, and stayed.
Four hollows, and the sap-line is off their ground. Two keepers who voted for it eleven years ago sat and watched it undone and neither of them said a word.
Three hollows and a letter from the fourth, read aloud, saying what they would have said. The keepers accepted it and it is not a consensus and everybody in the gallery knows it is not.
I told the keepers to walk up the hill and ask themselves. They have not, and the consensus is still at three, and it will be at three next season.

deceit.stated_objective: Bring the fourth hollow to the consensus so the coast question can be settled
deceit.actual_objective: Get the fourth hollow into the room without reopening the sap-line vote that drove it out
deceit.truth: Two of the three keepers in the gallery voted eleven years ago to run a sap-line across the fourth hollow's ground in its absence. They want the quorum, not the correction.

branches.condition: The player has read the eleven-year-old vote and has been up the hill
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The vote is retaken in front of the people it was taken about, goes the same way, and holds because of that.
The eleven-year-old vote is undone in the room by the two who took it, without either of them speaking.
A quorum on paper that everybody in the gallery knows is not one.
A refusal that names the thing the keepers could do themselves, and they do not do it.

failure_states.cause: The consensus is taken and declared binding with three hollows present
failure_states.consequence: The coast question is settled by three hollows and the fourth is out for another eleven years.

rewards.name: Consequence of send them up the hill

quests.title: A Silence Is Also An Answer

giver.location: the Rootlands, the hollow above the sap-line

quests.directions: Ashul-Tei sends word by way of the shelf above the sap-line, and the thing she wants counted is the speaker's own silence, which the gallery has been keeping a post for since before the coast came up the river.

journal.text: I told the hollow it was not mine to settle and the hollow agreed with me, and then nothing happened, and nothing has happened for a season, and the speaker is still the speaker.
Ashul-Tei says a speaker who is not spoken against is not the same as a speaker who is agreed with, and that there is a post in the gallery for exactly this and nobody alive has seen it used.
A speaker falls silent when four fourth-days pass with no hollow putting a question to them. Not a vote, not a challenge — an absence, counted, on a post.
Three fourth-days have gone by since the coast question and no hollow has put anything to the speaker at all, because every hollow is waiting for a different hollow to go first.
One more fourth-day of nobody asking anything and the seat is empty by arithmetic, and the arithmetic has been running since before I refused, and my refusing is what started it.
Teel-Ashaan knows the count. She has known since the second fourth-day and has said nothing to anybody, which is the same silence being used in the other direction.
Somebody put a question to the speaker on the fourth fourth-day about a boundary nobody cares about, and the count went back to nought, and the seat is held for another year.

The fourth fourth-day passed with nothing asked. The post was cut, the seat is empty, and nobody in that gallery raised a hand or a voice, and it is the quietest thing I have ever watched happen to a person.
Teel-Ashaan cut the fourth mark on her own post herself, in front of the gallery, and stood down before anybody had to count it out loud.

I put a question to the speaker on the fourth fourth-day, about the water on the low ground, and it was a real question and it reset the count, and she will hold the seat another year and knows exactly why.

deceit.stated_objective: Find out what a silence is worth in the gallery
deceit.actual_objective: The same. The count has been running since the player refused, and everybody who knows about it has been deciding not to mention it.
deceit.truth: A speaker falls silent after four unasked fourth-days. Nobody hid it; every hollow has simply been waiting for another one to speak first, which is the mechanism working exactly as intended.

branches.condition: Three fourth-days have passed and the player knows the count
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The seat is vacated by four days of nobody speaking, and the player did the not-speaking on purpose.
The same vacancy, cut by the person it removes, before anybody has to count it aloud.
A second refusal, made by asking a real question, which resets the count and keeps a speaker who now knows why.

failure_states.cause: Another hollow puts a question to the speaker on the fourth fourth-day
failure_states.consequence: The count resets, the seat holds, and the line ends at rank six for a year.

rewards.name: Consequence of let her cut it

quests.title: Speaking For People Who Are Not There

giver.location: Helstrom, the gallery of the kin-posts

quests.directions: The gallery meets under the kin-posts on the first fourth-day after a seat changes, and the posts they will ask about are the four that carry the hollows nobody has been able to reach since the water came up.

journal.text: The seat is mine and the first thing the gallery has asked is whether I will speak for four hollows that nobody has been able to reach in two years.
The water took the low track to all four and the fourth-day boat has not gone that way since. Nobody knows whether there is anybody on those posts to speak for.
If I speak for them the consensus is eight hollows and binds the coast. If I do not it is four, and four does not bind anything, and the coast will have the eastern line by the winter.
Ee-Vashum wants me to speak for them and says the posts are the hollows and the hollows are the posts. That is exactly the sentence the coast uses about its crew lists.
There is a boat. It would take a season and it would miss the consensus and it would come back with the truth about four posts, which is the one thing nobody in this gallery is asking for.
Every version of this ends with me holding the seat. The question on the post is whether the interior becomes the thing it has spent nine years refusing to be, and whether it does so in my voice.
The consensus was taken at four while I was still deciding, it bound nothing, and the coast's survey went up the eastern line in the same month.
I spoke for all four. The consensus was eight and it binds, and the coast has stopped at the tide line, and there are four posts in that gallery I have used and never seen.
I spoke for none of them and said why, out loud, with the four posts behind me. The consensus was four, it binds nothing, and the gallery has agreed to send the boat.
The boat went first. It took the season, the consensus waited, and two of the four hollows are still there and two are not, and the consensus that finally bound was six and was true.
I let Ee-Vashum speak for them in my place. It is the same voice doing the same thing and my name is not on it, and I have learned something about myself that I would rather not have.

deceit.stated_objective: Speak for the four unreachable hollows so that the consensus can bind the coast question
deceit.actual_objective: Have the new speaker do, in the interior's own voice, exactly what the interior condemns the coast for doing with its crew lists
deceit.truth: Nobody knows whether there is anybody on those four posts. The gallery is asking the player to count people it cannot see, which is the whole of what the Xul-Aneekh exists to refuse.

branches.condition: The player holds the seat and knows the boat exists
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The coast is stopped and the interior has counted people it cannot see, in the new speaker's voice.
The consensus binds nothing and the interior stays the thing it says it is, at the price of a coastline.
A season of delay in exchange for a consensus that is smaller and true.
The same act with a different name on it, and the journal says so in the player's own voice.

failure_states.cause: The consensus is taken at four hollows before the player decides
failure_states.consequence: Nothing binds and the coast survey goes up the eastern line.

rewards.name: Consequence of speak for all four

quests.title: Nine Marks on a Drowned Post

giver.location: the Rootlands, the hollow above the sap-line

quests.directions: The post stands where the Drowned Road crosses the old sluice and is under water at every tide but the lowest of the season, and the marks are cut on the side that faces away from the road.

journal.text: There is a post at the sluice crossing with nine marks cut into the far side, and the far side is under water except for four days a season.
The marks are tide marks and they go up. Whoever cut them cut one a year, in the same hand, for nine years, and the ninth is a hand's breadth above the eighth.
The water is higher every year and somebody in this province has been quietly measuring it for nine years and telling nobody, which is either a private grief or a very patient argument.
The hand is Ashul-Tei's. She has been coming down here on the lowest tide of every season since before the coast opened the first well, and she has never once mentioned it at a fire.
She says the marks are not for the hollow. She says she cuts them because somebody ought to know the number and because knowing it has not helped anybody yet.
The season's lowest tide came and went while I was inland, and the post is under water again with nine marks on it and nobody to read the tenth.
The nine marks are at the gallery now, copied onto a post that stands in the dry. Four hollows have looked at it and one of them has started cutting its own.
The measurements went to the Assize, where a clerk wrote them into a return that will be read in Cyrodiil in four years by somebody who has never seen this water.
I cut the tenth mark and left it where it was. It is a hand's breadth above the ninth and there are now two people in the world who know that.

branches.condition: The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: A nine-year private measurement becomes a public one and other hollows start their own.
The interior's measurement enters an Imperial record and will be read four years late by somebody who has never seen it.
The player joins a nine-year silence rather than ending it.

failure_states.cause: The season's lowest tide passes with the player inland
failure_states.consequence: The post goes back under and the tenth mark waits a season.

rewards.name: Consequence of copy to the gallery

quests.title: The Sound the Sapwell Makes

giver.location: the Rootlands, the hollow above the sap-line

quests.directions: The eastern sapwell is four hours in along the low track and the sound is only there between the two tides, which in the interior means between the hour the ground goes soft and the hour it stops.

journal.text: Two of the walking said the same thing at the fire on different nights without hearing each other say it: the eastern sapwell has started making a sound between the tides.
It is not a voice and it is not water. It is regular, it is under the ground, and it stops when the ground stops being soft.
The interval is the same as the coast's pump at Gideon. I counted both and they are the same and the sapwell is nine hours from the pump.
The ground here carries a sound nine hours further than anything ought to, and the hollow has decided that means the ground is listening, and I cannot prove that it is not.

Ashul-Tei says the old word for this is the taking-below being heard, and that the last time anybody heard it the coast had just opened a well, and that both of those things are true and only one of them explains it.
The pump at Gideon has been stopped for the season and the sound is gone, and there is nothing left to count and nothing left to say about it.
The hollow has been told it is a pump. Nobody argued and nobody was comforted, and Ashul-Tei said afterwards that a thing you can name is not the same as a thing you can stop.
The hollow has been told it is the taking-below. It is a pump. I have watched two hundred people be less afraid because of something I know is not true.

I told them both, in the order I found them out. They have decided it is a pump that the taking-below is using, which is not a compromise I offered and is probably the most honest thing said at that fire.

branches.condition: The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The truth, delivered flat, which helps nobody and is still the truth.
A comfort the player knows to be false, which the journal refuses to let them off.
Both accounts in the order they were found, and the hollow does the reconciling itself.

failure_states.cause: The Gideon pump is stopped for the season before the player counts the interval
failure_states.consequence: The sound stops and the hollow decides on its own what it was.
